items.difficulty_reason: The counted unit is the author's own proposition unioncardinalscardinal at source lines 691-693: if every member of X is a cardinal, then the union of X is a cardinal. The proof at source lines 695-703 does not follow from the definition of a cardinal by a single unfolding. It first has to be seen that the union of X is an ordinal, which is left to the reader as an easy check because unions of ordinals are ordinals, and the real content is the second half: given an ordinal alpha in the union of X, one must find a cardinal b in X with alpha in b, use that b is a cardinal to conclude alpha is strictly smaller than b as a cardinal, then use b subseteq union X to obtain that b is at most union X, and chain the two strict/smaller comparisons to conclude alpha is not equinumerous with union X. The proof uses three distinct closure facts (union of ordinals, subset of a union, transitivity of the cardinal comparison) and the generalisation step at the end is what converts the pointwise statement into the cardinality assertion. No result outside the retained text is used.
